content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is reportedly set to be announced in just over two weeks. Despite possibly being named the "iPhone Ultra" and priced over $2,000, it will come with several major limitations.

#1: Telephoto Lens

The iPhone Ultra is reportedly set to feature two cameras, including a main lens and an ultrawide lens, but a telephoto lens is not expected. For many people, this may be the most obvious design limitation of the device.

Both the main lens and ultrawide lens of the iPhone Ultra are reportedly set to be 48-megapixel, similar to the current standard iPhone 17.

#2: Action Button

Based on multiple leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units, this device will not feature an Action button. In fact, it appears to be the first iPhone in Apple's history to have no silent switch whatsoever.

The dummy units show that the left side of the device is completely blank. The side button and camera control button are reportedly set to be placed on the right edge of the iPhone Ultra, while the volume keys will be positioned on the top edge, similar to the iPad mini.

#3: Face ID

The iPhone Ultra is reportedly not set to feature Face ID, but will instead integrate Touch ID into the side button. This would mark the first time Apple has released an iPhone without Face ID since Face ID debuted on the iPhone X in 2017.

The reason the iPhone Ultra is switching to Touch ID rather than Face ID is most likely due to the device's ultra-thin design. Additionally, Apple would need to equip two sets of Face ID components, one for the outer display and one for the inner display.

Apple still uses Touch ID on the power button of most iPads, including the standard iPad, iPad mini, and iPad Air.

#4: MagSafe

Although Apple may surprise everyone, it appears the iPhone Ultra will not support MagSafe wireless charging. The leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units show no MagSafe magnetic ring on the back.

The iPhone Ultra may offer standard wireless charging similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 foldable phone, but based on current rumours, MagSafe seems more difficult to implement.

#5: Physical SIM Card

According to multiple sources including Kuo Ming-Chi and Bloomberg, the iPhone Ultra will support eSIM only worldwide.

This approach is most likely due to the extremely thin body design of the foldable iPhone. Like the iPhone Air, which also has an extremely thin body, it supports eSIM only worldwide. As for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, they support eSIM only in the United States and some other countries, while retaining a physical SIM card slot in markets such as China.

Summary

Obviously, Apple's foldable iPhone Ultra will involve major trade-offs across multiple features. The question is whether the practicality brought by the innovative foldable design is enough to compensate for the shortcomings in other areas.

Personally speaking, I'm really looking forward to trying the iPhone Ultra. The trade-off that concerns me the most is the lack of MagSafe. I'm currently using the iPhone Air, so I've already gotten used to life without a telephoto lens. I think I can adapt to Touch ID quite easily. However, my home and office are filled with MagSafe chargers everywhere, so going back to using regular wireless charging or wired charging all the time would be a significant change for me.
